subject: Follow-up: Streamly POC — throughput, continuous batching & $/1M estimate
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Novak <anya@streamly.io>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver@streamly.io>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Streamly POC — throughput, continuous batching & $/1M estimate

Hi Anya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned before the POC kickoff. I copied Oliver per your request.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary workload: live personalization for video streams (captioning + short-form recommendations).
- Current traffic shape: big spikes in evenings (US PST), regular daytime baseline. You mentioned typical concurrent viewers translate to ~150 active inference sessions at peak.
- Typical prompt/response size you expect: request ~80–160 tokens, response ~50–300 tokens depending on the feature.

Open items I need from you to finalize the POC config and cost estimate:
1) Monthly token volume range (best-effort): low / expected / high.
2) Target budget band for initial POC ($ per 1M tokens target is helpful).
3) Latency SLO: 95p target (ms) and whether sub-200ms is required for the recommendation path.
4) Concurrency expectations during peak 10-minute windows and steady-state.
5) A 30–60 minute sample of production traffic (anonymized) if you can — helps us size batching windows.

My initial assumptions for the POC (please correct):
- Monthly tokens: 15M (low) / 35M (expected) / 80M (high).
- Goal budget: $50–$90 per 1M tokens for POC (including limited cache/batching optimizations).
- Target latency: 95p <= 250ms for captioning path; recommendation path target 95p <= 200ms.
- Continuous batching: we expect meaningful batching on the recommendation path during daytime baseline; less effective in low-fanout bursts. We'll size for a 100–250ms batching window initially and iterate.

Attachments: draft POC plan (streamly_poc_plan.pdf) and an inputs checklist.

Next steps / asks
- You: confirm the 5 items above + share the traffic sample (streamly_traffic_sample.csv) if possible.
- Us (Redwood): we'll return a POC config + expected rough $/1M tokens and recommended instance sizing within 48 business hours once we have your sample.

If all sounds right, we'll schedule a 30-min kickoff next Tue to lock the test harness.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachment: streamly_poc_plan.pdf (3 pages summary)
From: Anya Novak <anya@streamly.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver@streamly.io>, Streamly Ops <ops@streamly.io>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 17:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Streamly POC — throughput, continuous batching & $/1M estimate

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers below, attached a 48-hr sampled CSV of anonymized requests (streamly_traffic_sample.csv).

Answers:
- Monthly tokens (approx): 10M / 28M / 65M (low/expected/high).
- Budget for POC: prefer to keep below $60 per 1M tokens; can stretch to $75 if latency improvements are material.
- Latency SLOs: captioning 95p <= 300ms (can tolerate slightly higher); recommender 95p <= 200ms (hard requirement during peak).
- Concurrency: steady-state 25–40 concurrent inference sessions; peak 120–170 concurrent (10–15 minute peaks during major live events).

Notes on traffic shape (from Oliver): bursts are highly correlated to show start times and chat spikes; many short requests during bursts (median request token ~110).

We're fine with a 100–200ms batching window if you think that'll preserve recommender latency.

Let's target Wednesday for the kickoff if you can deliver the POC config tomorrow.

Cheers,
Anya Novak
Head of Product, Streamly
anya@streamly.io

Attachment: streamly_traffic_sample.csv (48-hour anonymized sample)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: Streamly POC — throughput, continuous batching & $/1M estimate

Forwarding Streamly's answers + sample. Key asks for us: run a quick sizing + cost calc for a 4-week POC and propose an initial batching/concurrency config we can present tomorrow.

Highlights from Anya:
- Monthly tokens expected ~28M (cap to 65M high); target budget < $60 / 1M tokens (can go to $75 if latency improves).
- Peak concurrency 120–170, baseline 25–40. Median request ~110 tokens.
- Recommender path 95p <= 200ms is non-negotiable for them.

Assumptions I'd like you to validate and return asap:
1) Effective token rate after batching & KV cache for recommender: assume 30–45% token amortization (i.e. effective tokens billed lower due to batching/prefix reuse).
2) POC traffic shape: use sample but simulate 15-minute peaks at 170 concurrent with same median token sizes.
3) Instance sizing: recommend GPU + concurrency slab and whether q8_0 or q4_0 quantization path acceptable for quality.
4) Ballpark $/1M tokens for the 4-week POC (show low/expected/high) and a 99% upper bound for cost in case bursts are more costly.

Please include a short slide (1–2) or spreadsheet (redwood_poc_costs.xlsx) with the calc. Marissa: pinging you for approval if the $/1M falls within our POC discount bands.

Thanks — need this within ~4 business hours to make the Wed kickoff.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: Streamly POC — throughput, continuous batching & $/1M estimate

Quick first-pass numbers below (will attach formal spreadsheet in 1hr):
- Assumed model: open-recommendation-2.1 (gen), avg request+response 200 tokens.
- Baseline effective token amortization: 35% (continuous batching + KV reuse) => effective billed tokens ~130 per inference.
- POC sizing: 2x dedciated GPU workers (A100-equivalent), continuous batching window 150ms, autoscale ramp for peaks to 4x.
- Ballpark cost: low $/1M = $42; expected $/1M = $58; high $/1M = $95 (high assumes poor batching during bursts + model fallback).
- 99% upper bound for the 4-week POC: $12,400 (includes peak burst multipliers, infrequent fallback to larger model).

I'll send redwood_poc_costs.xlsx and a 2-slide summary in 45 minutes. If Marissa signs off on the POC discount (we can offer 20% off expected), expected comes down to ~$46 / 1M.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
